## Summary

The full 2026-05-03 guide describes taking an initial CHF payment, having the customer authorize future use of TWINT, and saving the resulting TWINT PaymentMethod for later off-session payments. Before reuse, associate the method with the same customer identity. The examples distinguish an Accounts v2 customer-configured Account (`customer_account`) from a Customers v1 Customer (`customer`). The May guide describes Accounts v2 as generally available to Connect users and in public preview for other Stripe users, who must specify a preview version when participating.

## Initial payment and authorization

- **Hosted Checkout.** Create a server-side payment-mode Checkout Session with CHF line items, TWINT, the customer identity and `payment_intent_data.setup_future_usage=off_session`. The customer authorizes future use through Checkout. Retrieve the Session’s PaymentIntent and `payment_method` via the `checkout.session.completed` event or retrieve the Session with the ID in the `success_url`. The redirect supplies a lookup path. It can be visited directly or missed when the customer closes the browser.
- **Elements.** Set `setup_future_usage=off_session` on the server-created PaymentIntent and use its client secret. The May web examples use `stripe.confirmPayment()` with `return_url`.
- **Direct API.** The May guide illustrates `payment_method_data.type=twint` and `setup_future_usage=off_session`. The client route uses `stripe.confirmTwintPayment()` with the PaymentIntent secret and `return_url`. The optional server-confirmed route supplies `mandate_data`, with IP address and user agent in the example’s online acceptance data, plus `return_url`. When the Intent is `requires_action`, send the customer to `next_action.redirect_to_url.url` to authorize with TWINT.

Verify mandate authorization from Stripe state or verified events. The May guide instructs merchants to save the resulting `payment_method` ID after `payment_intent.succeeded` and describes `payment_intent.payment_failed` with the Intent returning to `requires_payment_method` when authorization fails.

## Later off-session charging

List the customer’s attached `twint` methods and create and confirm a new CHF PaymentIntent with the matching customer and saved method IDs, `off_session=true` and `confirm=true`. The May guide makes `return_url` optional specifically for a TWINT method already set up by a SetupIntent or a PaymentIntent with `setup_future_usage`.

## Detail locators

- May raw lines 8–324 cover hosted Checkout, lookup, mandate events and reuse. Lines 331–864 cover Elements. Lines 866–1222 cover Direct API, including both confirmation paths.
- May sandbox examples describe authorization changing `requires_action` to `succeeded` or `requires_payment_method`. The May Direct API test fixtures at lines 1209–1222 simulate generic decline and mandate revocation. They use the spelling `payment_intent.failed`, while the guide’s general authorization monitor at lines 1129–1135 names `payment_intent.payment_failed`. The fixture spelling leaves the event contract unverified.

payments-twint-save-during-payment.text: This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:
To reuse a TWINT payment method for future payments, attach it to an object that represents your customer.

The `return_url` parameter isn’t required when using a TWINT payment method that was previously set up with a SetupIntent or a PaymentIntent with `setup_future_usage`. It’s required for all other cases.

payments-twint-save-during-payment.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/twint/save-during-payment offers only Checkout, Elements and Direct API routes for saving TWINT details during an initial payment (new raw lines 5-15). The May 3, 2026 guide associates the TWINT method with a Customers v1 Customer or a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account with dated access/version qualifications. Hosted Checkout uses a payment-mode Session with CHF items and nested setup_future_usage=off_session (old raw lines 29-43 and 75-160). Elements uses stripe.confirmPayment, while Direct API uses stripe.confirmTwintPayment or server-side confirmation with mandate_data and requires_action redirect_to_url to let the customer authorize (old raw lines 659-704 and 1050-1127). Verify mandate authorization through Stripe state/events, not a browser return. May describes succeeded with payment_intent.succeeded and requires_payment_method with payment_intent.payment_failed, and the merchant stores the resulting attached payment method on success. A later off-session payment is a separate confirmed PaymentIntent with matching customer and saved method identifiers (old raw lines 1129-1207). source-stripe-twint-save-during-payment.md now spells out the attachment, result verification and prior setup condition for the return_url exception. The selector contributes no fresh transaction evidence.
payments-twint-save-during-payment.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/twint/save-during-payment, the November 7, 2026 change is presentational and navigation-only. Its three child routes are the same variants declared in the May 3, 2026 guide (new raw lines 9-15, old raw lines 8-14, 331-337, and 866-872). Preserve dated May Accounts v2/Customers v1 distinctions and the initial customer authorization, redirect-versus-confirmation warning, successful and failed events and saved-method reuse with return_url exemption only for prior SetupIntent or PaymentIntent with setup_future_usage (old raw lines 29-43, 162-178, and 242-324). The Direct API's dated test payment_intent.failed spelling differs from payment_intent.payment_failed in the general monitoring guidance (old raw lines 1129-1135 and 1209-1222). The revised source-stripe-twint-save-during-payment.md makes those previously omitted scope distinctions and keeps the November index in navigation. Preserve the May raw, root-to-Stripe provider index, TWINT concept's reciprocal source route and separate setup-only and acceptance navigation. The November links do not reverify linked behavior.
